clue.text: Stop holding money for a fool

indicators.note: holding means the first word's letters wrap round the second piece

parts.note: a full stop is a dot
L is the abbreviation for pound, a sum of money (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to hand over cash to a simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Harangued the underworld boss and then ran!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
coursed means ran or flowed swiftly

explanation.surface: Someone shouted at a mafia chief and then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a gangster; it is the classical ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to speak at length, so to have lectured someone or harangued them.

clue.text: The Franco-British craftsman's machine

parts.note: la is French for the
the English word itself, as British usage gives it

explanation.surface: A machine used by a craftsman of Anglo-French origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is read twice: once in French (la), once in English.
explanation.definitionFit: A turner shapes wood or metal on a rotating machine tool, used by craftsmen.

clue.text: Fussy detail

explanation.surface: A pernickety person fusses over small points.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular means hard to please (fussy) and, as a noun, a single item or point (a detail).

clue.text: Manila's wild creatures

indicators.note: wild means the letters of Manila's run riot into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is used as a letter here

explanation.surface: The untamed wildlife of the Philippine capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals are living creatures, beasts.

clue.text: Went uncertainly to minister — went in advance

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by a minister of religion
led means went in front, guided

explanation.surface: Someone shuffled hesitantly over to a clergyman who walked ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler walks with short unsteady steps, so toddled means walked uncertainly.

clue.text: Island in the South Pacific. A primitive tribe lives there

indicators.note: in says the answer is found inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: An island in the South Seas inhabited by a primitive tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Pacific is a false lead: the island is in the Bay of Naples, sitting across the end of Pacific and A pri-.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an island off Naples in Italy.

clue.text: Richard the Liar? No, that's not right!

indicators.note: not right says the letters of the Liar No are wrongly ordered and must be reset

explanation.surface: Someone protests that King Richard was no liar.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I of England was nicknamed the Lionheart for his courage.

clue.text: The sort of knot sailors consider dangerous

explanation.surface: Sailors are wary of a certain knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a square knot used for tying sails; a reef is a ridge of rock or coral that can wreck ships.

clue.text: Proceeds when attention is shown

explanation.surface: Profits come once people pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is money earned on capital (proceeds) and also concern or curiosity shown towards something.

clue.text: An Australian winger brooded in prison

parts.note: a hen that brooded sat on her eggs
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: Someone sat moping while locked up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' is a bird, not a sports player or a politician; 'doing bird' is British slang for serving time in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The satin bird is the satin bowerbird, a bird (a winged creature) of eastern Australia.

clue.text: Quiet dress, but sound

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a robe is a long dress or gown

explanation.surface: A plain, muted outfit that is nonetheless in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy; it is the verb, to sound out or test the depth of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound something is to investigate or test it, a synonym for to probe it.

clue.text: Order and start selling fat

annotationWithheld.why: Order and start selling fat (5) as held: OBE (Order) plus S (start of selling) gives only OBES; no clue word supplies the final E, so the clue looks cut or misread and no scan is available.

clue.text: No-one left? That's good!

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether anybody remains and is pleased to find the place empty.
explanation.definitionFit: If no-one is on the left, everyone is on the right; all right is also an exclamation of approval, like OK.

clue.text: A negotiator will find the answer in farm equipment

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a tractor is a farm vehicle
ANS is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: A dealer finds the solution in a piece of farm machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A transactor is one who conducts business, such as a negotiator of deals.

clue.text: Organised crime, being bats

explanation.surface: Gangsters arrive armed with clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are criminal schemes such as extortion, and also the strung bats used in tennis or squash.

clue.text: Figure maybe he's an eccentric individual

explanation.surface: A man described as an odd type.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol such as a figure, and also an odd or colourful person.

clue.text: An unhappy state, though it might be praised

indicators.note: might be says the word praised could be turned into something else by reordering its letters

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable despite being complimented.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deeply unhappy condition.

clue.text: Joint twice turned over and the stripper put inside

indicators.note: put inside says one piece is placed within the other
turned over says the word for twice is read backwards

parts.note: bis is Latin and musical for twice, a call for a repeat
a parer is a tool or person that strips off peel

explanation.surface: A nightclub stripper is twice overturned at the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripper' is not a performer but a peeler; 'joint' is a cut of meat, not a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare rib is a cut of pork from the ribs, a joint of meat.

clue.text: Allowing for expansion

parts.note: describes a material or a rule that can stretch to take in more, as a waistband or a flexible budget does

explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can be pulled out and returns to shape, so it allows for expansion.

clue.text: Distorted rail cut to make shorter

indicators.note: distorted says the letters of rail cut are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A warped length of rail is trimmed to size.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short or reduce in length.

clue.text: Begin with lead weight

parts.note: the lead in a film or play is its star
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone starts off carrying a heavy plumb weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the heavy metal, which suits 'weight'; it is the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To start on something is to begin working with it, as in starting on dinner.

clue.text: An academician's jacket

explanation.surface: A member of the Academy wears a particular jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: An academician is a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Stanley Spencer was a painter and Royal Academician; a spencer is also a short close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Drink where tunes are rendered

indicators.note: rendered means the letters of tunes are are performed in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bar where music is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Hook stock

explanation.surface: Someone hooks the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a hooked claw; in card games the talon is the stock of undealt cards.

clue.text: Offering some pretext, radioed for additional supplies

indicators.note: Offering some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone radios in an excuse in order to get more provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual, so extra supplies are additional ones.

clue.text: Getting explosive about dealing with running water

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: TNT is the explosive trinitrotoluene
re means concerning or dealing with

explanation.surface: Someone becomes angry about how flowing water is managed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a river, a body of running water.

clue.text: The medico goes in like a man

indicators.note: goes in says the medical officer is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: as means like
MO, medical officer, is a doctor or medico

explanation.surface: The doctor enters looking like a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a man's name, borne by the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Copper possibly ran into new driver

annotationWithheld.why: Copper possibly ran into new driver (5) as held: MET (ran into) plus L (new driver) gives only METL; no clue word supplies the A, so a word such as 'a' looks lost in OCR and no scan is available.
annotationWithheld.clue: Copper possibly ran into new driver

clue.text: A person with constructive ideas for the use of the Arctic

indicators.note: making use of the words the Arctic means their letters are put to work in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone plans buildings for polar regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A building designer has ideas about construction, punning on constructive meaning helpful.

clue.text: They'll put the squeeze on many among the aliens

indicators.note: among says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: aliens are foreigners or strangers
L is the Roman numeral fifty, standing for many

explanation.surface: Many foreigners are being pressured.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrotters kill by throttling, literally squeezing the neck.

clue.text: A way tax administrators cause agitation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: Tax collectors find a method of making trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax-collecting department until 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to stir up trouble, to provoke agitation.
